'''Raoul Bricard''' (23 March 1870 – 26 November 1943) was a French [[engineer]] and a [[mathematician]].  He is best known for his work in [[geometry]], especially [[descriptive geometry]] and [[scissors congruence]], and [[kinematics]], especially [[mechanical linkage]]s.

== Biography ==
Bricard taught geometry at [[Ecole Centrale des Arts et Manufactures]].  In 1908 he became a professor of applied geometry at the [[Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers|National Conservatory of Arts and Crafts]] in [[Paris]].<ref>''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', vol. 28 (1908), p. 707.</ref> In 1932 he received the [[Poncelet Prize]] in [[mathematics]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences|Paris Academy of Sciences]] for his work in geometry.<ref>[http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v131/n3301/abs/131174a0.html "Prize Awards of the Paris Academy of Sciences"], ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' vol. 131 (1933) 174-175.</ref>

== Work ==
In 1896 Bricard published a paper on [[Hilbert's third problem]], even before the problem was stated by [[David Hilbert|Hilbert]].<ref>R. Bricard, "Sur une question de géométrie relative aux polyèdres", ''[[Nouvelles Annales de Mathématiques|Nouvelles annales de mathématiques]]'', Ser. 3, Vol. 15 (1896), 331-334.</ref>  In it he proved that [[Reflection symmetry|mirror symmetric]] [[polytope]]s are [[scissors congruence|scissors congruent]], and proved a weak version of [[Max Dehn|Dehn]]'s criterion.

[[File:Br1-anim.gif|thumb|One of the [[Bricard octahedron|Bricard octahedra]]]]
In 1897 Bricard published an important investigation on [[flexible polyhedra]].<ref>R. Bricard, [http://www-mathdoc.ujf-grenoble.fr/JMPA/PDF/JMPA_1897_5_3_A5_0.pdf Mémoire sur la théorie de l’octaèdre articulé] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717152710/http://www-mathdoc.ujf-grenoble.fr/JMPA/PDF/JMPA_1897_5_3_A5_0.pdf |date=2011-07-17 }}, ''J. Math. Pures Appl.'', Vol. 3 (1897), 113–150 (see also the [http://math.unm.edu/~vageli/papers/bricard3_6.pdf English translation] and an [https://archive.org/details/s5journaldemat03liou/page/113/ alternative scan]).</ref> In it he classified all flexible [[octahedron|octahedra]], now known as [[Bricard octahedron|Bricard octahedra]].<ref>P. Cromwell, ''Polyhedra'', [[Cambridge University Press]], 1997.</ref> This work was the subject of [[Henri Lebesgue|Henri Lebesgue's]] lectures in 1938.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Lebesgue H. | authorlink = Henri Lebesgue | year = 1967| title = Octaedres articules de Bricard | doi=10.5169/seals-41541 | journal = Enseign. Math. |series=Series 2 | volume = 13 | issue = 3| pages = 175–185 }}</ref> Later Bricard discovered notable 6-bar linkages.<ref>K. Wohlhart, The two types of the orthogonal Bricard linkage, ''Mechanism and machine theory'',  vol. 28 (1993), 809-817.</ref><ref>{{YouTube|fO1OI-YZS3Y|Bricard 6 Bar Linkage Origami}}.</ref>

Bricard also gave one of the first geometric proofs of [[Morley's trisector theorem]] in 1922.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Guy Richard K. |authorlink=Richard K. Guy |year=2007 |title=The Lighthouse Theorem, Morley & Malfatti - A Budget of Paradoxes |url=http://math.ucalgary.ca/files/publications/3414848.pdf | jstor = 27642143 |journal=[[American Mathematical Monthly]] |volume=114 |issue=2 |pages=97–141 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419064244/http://math.ucalgary.ca/files/publications/3414848.pdf |archivedate=April 19, 2012 |doi=10.1080/00029890.2007.11920398 |s2cid=46275242 }}</ref><ref>[[Alain Connes]], [http://www.ems-ph.org/journals/newsletter/pdf/2004-12-54.pdf "Symmetries"], ''[[European Mathematical Society]] Newsletter'' No. 54 (December 2004).</ref>

== Books ==
Bricard authored six books, including a mathematics survey in [[Esperanto]].<ref>[https://openlibrary.org/a/OL743075A Raoul Bricard], from [[Open Library]].</ref> He is listed in ''[[Encyclopedia of Esperanto]]''.<ref>[http://www.freeweb.hu/eventoj/steb/gxenerala_naturscienco/enciklopedio-1/encikl.htm Encyclopedia of Esperanto] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218101913/http://www.freeweb.hu/eventoj/steb/gxenerala_naturscienco/enciklopedio-1/encikl.htm |date=2008-12-18 }}</ref>
* ''Matematika terminaro kaj krestomatio'' (in Esperanto), Hachette, Paris, 1905
* [http://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000662067 ''Géométrie descriptive''], O. Doin et fils, 1911
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=Grs3AAAAMAAJ ''Cinématique et mécanismes''], A. Colin, 1921
* ''Petit traité de perspective'', Vuibert, 1924<ref>{{cite journal|author=Emch, Arnold|authorlink=Arnold Emch|title=Review: ''Petit Traité de Perspective'' by Raoul Bricard|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1925|volume=31|issue=9|pages=564–565|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1925-31-09/S0002-9904-1925-04125-7/S0002-9904-1925-04125-7.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1925-04125-7}}</ref>
*[http://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k879032k  ''Leçons de cinématique''], Gauthier-Villars et cie., 1926
*[http://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000469108 ''Le calcul vectoriel''], A. Colin, 1929
